questions.prompt: In this course, what does 'Operation' mainly cover?
questions.explanation: Development = code, review, debug, refactor, document. Operation = automation, infrastructure, monitoring, deployment.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a property of a good algorithm?
questions.explanation: A good algorithm is clear, has defined inputs/outputs, is feasible, finite and language independent.

questions.prompt: An algorithm is designed for humans to understand, a program for computers to execute.
questions.explanation: Algorithm = step-by-step instructions (a recipe); program = the functional element a computer runs (the cake).

questions.prompt: 2 bits can represent 4 values. How many values can 3 bits represent?
1 byte is equal to how many bits?
What is the time complexity of this loop?
questions.explanation: The loop body runs n times, so it grows linearly with n.

questions.prompt: Halving the problem at every step (e.g. binary search) typically gives which complexity?
questions.explanation: Divide-and-conquer that halves the input each step takes log n steps.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm strategy tries ALL possible options?
questions.explanation: Brute force = try all the options. Greedy picks the locally best option.

questions.prompt: Solving Sudoku by placing one number at a time and undoing dead ends is…
questions.explanation: Backtracking builds a solution piece by piece and discards partial solutions that fail (Sudoku example on the slide).

questions.prompt: What is 'information' compared to raw data?
options: Raw data in its basic digital form
Data that has been processed and has meaning
questions.explanation: Information is processed data that carries meaning; raw data is the basic digital form.

questions.prompt: Continuous Integration: a new feature must pass which checks?
questions.explanation: CI = the new feature passes build, lint (rules) and tests before it is integrated.

questions.prompt: In the DevOps toolchain from the lecture, Kibana is used for…
questions.explanation: Monitoring & logging: Kibana visualises data/performance and logs the live system.

questions.prompt: According to the course rules, how should you use AI?
options: To generate homework code for you
Never, not even to ask questions
As a tutor/reviewer - and double-check what it says
questions.explanation: Use AI to review and to understand content, not to generate your work - and always double-check it.
